title: Multi-Head Attention & Rotary Position Embeddings
summary: Run several attention heads at once by slicing the feature axis, and give attention a sense of order by rotating queries and keys with RoPE, so scores depend only on how far apart two tokens are.
takeaways: Heads are slices of the feature axis: reshape (B, T, D) to (B, T, H, d_head), then transpose to (B, H, T, d_head).
Reshaping without the transpose gives the right shape but the wrong heads, and nothing errors.
RoPE rotates each feature pair of q and k by position × θᵢ, with θᵢ = 10000^(−2i/d_head).
Rotations preserve norms, and rotated q·k depends only on the offset m − n: absolute rotations, relative scores.

flow.title: One multi-head attention layer with RoPE

steps.label: Project
steps.detail: Q, K, V = X W_q, X W_k, X W_v, each (B, T, D).

steps.label: Split heads
steps.detail: Reshape to (B, T, H, d_head) and transpose to (B, H, T, d_head).

steps.label: Rotate
steps.detail: Apply RoPE to Q and K (not V) using each token's position.

steps.label: Attend per head
steps.detail: softmax(QKᵀ/√d_head) with an optional causal mask, times V.

steps.label: Merge + mix
steps.detail: Transpose back, reshape to (B, T, D), multiply by W_o.

terms.definition: One independent attention computation over its own d_head-dimensional slice of the projected features.
Per-head width, D / H. Scores are scaled by √d_head.
A (D, D) matrix that mixes the concatenated head outputs back into the model dimension.
Rotary position embedding: rotate feature pairs of q and k by an angle proportional to the token's position.
The offset m − n between two tokens. Under RoPE it's the only positional information the q·k score sees.
Two RoPE pairing conventions: (x₂ᵢ, x₂ᵢ₊₁) versus (xᵢ, xᵢ₊d/2). Same idea, incompatible weights.
